subject: glowworm
title: A Glowworm's Light Comes From Its Waste Organ, and It Is a Trap

scenes.text: Those glowing cave ceilings aren't stars. They're worms, and the light comes from their bottoms.
A New Zealand glowworm glows from the tip of its excretory system.
It hangs up to thirty sticky silk threads below it, like fishing lines.
Midges mistake the glow for the open sky, fly up, and get stuck.
It spends about a year as a hungry larva. The adult has no mouth and lives only a few days.
So that beautiful night sky is a field of traps, lit by waste.

description:
Those glowing cave ceilings aren't stars. They're worms.
A New Zealand glowworm makes light in its excretory system and uses it to lure midges into sticky silk threads.
Would you take a boat ride under a sky of glowworm traps? Comment below.
first_comment: Neighbouring glowworm larvae even sync their light to make a stronger display. Would you ride a boat under them?
